question: Summarize the documented symptom course during the episode and the reason for the additional individual contact on January 19. Which symptom assessments are distinct, and what conclusions about progress can and cannot be supported?

items.subject: measure:BH-D002:0

items.subject: HG-E101
items.text: Rowan Mercer attended an individual session for several weeks of low mood, reduced interest, fragmented sleep, and work-return worry with avoidance. Behavioral activation and a short work-task step were introduced; no immediate safety concern was identified. PHQ-9 total was 18.

items.subject: HG-E102
items.text: Coping skills group focused on recognizing early physical signs of anxiety and choosing a coping response before withdrawing from a task. Rowan Mercer participated, identified an avoidance situation involving a delayed work message, practiced paced breathing, and selected reading the message before responding as a possible next step.

items.subject: HG-E103
items.text: Patient did not check in for scheduled individual visit and was not seen; no arrival call or cancellation was received. Later callback addressed scheduling and contact information only; no therapy was conducted.

items.subject: HG-E104
items.text: Family psychotherapy session with Rowan Mercer and partner Casey Mercer, focused on patterns of support at home as Rowan works to rebuild a routine. The pair mapped a recent interaction, practiced specific help requests and reflective responses, and agreed on a planned check-in about work preparation.

items.subject: HG-E104
items.text: Family session with Rowan Mercer and Casey Mercer, facilitated by Leena Park, LPC, with Mara Voss, LCSW. Focus was on communication practice when slowing down an anxious exchange about the return-to-work process; both participants reflected each other's concerns and agreed on a brief predictable check-in and a shared evening walk.

items.subject: HG-E105
items.text: Group coping skills session on behavioral activation, activity ladders, obstacle anticipation, and rehearsing responses to missed attempts. Patient participated actively, identifying avoidance patterns and planning a concrete next action.

items.subject: HG-E106
items.text: Medication management visit for ongoing depressive and anxiety symptoms with sleep disruption. Rowan reported continuing sleep interruption, daytime tiredness, and work communication concerns; the medication list was reviewed and reconciled, and adherence and monitoring were discussed. No urgent medication concern was raised; no separate psychotherapy was provided.

items.subject: HG-E107
items.text: Individual psychotherapy session focused on identifying the prediction behind a delayed work-message reply and separating a brief acknowledgment from a commitment to a specific work schedule. The clinician and patient drafted and rehearsed a short response; patient reported completing several small activities, ongoing interrupted sleep, and effort with morning routines. Plan: attempt the drafted acknowledgment, continue morning activity tracking, and practice a breathing skill before avoided tasks.

items.subject: HG-E108
items.text: Coping skills group scheduled for January 15 was cancelled by the clinic due to staff illness; no group was held and no participants were seen. No replacement group was conducted in the slot.

items.subject: HG-E109
items.text: Family collateral contact with partner Casey Mercer only, after the patient advised they could not participate. Casey reported home observations and strategies to support the treatment plan; no patient-present psychotherapy occurred.

items.subject: HG-E110
items.text: Skills group on recognizing the sequence of trigger, anxious prediction, physical activation, and avoidance, using a worked example and practice selecting a small approach behavior. Rowan Mercer followed the exercise initially but became visibly tense when discussion turned to returning to the workplace and said it felt difficult to manage; the facilitator offered grounding and arranged a same-day individual meeting with the treating clinician.

items.subject: HG-E110
items.text: Rowan attended the opening check-in, accepted the exercise handout, and requested additional help from the individual clinician. Group content is recorded separately.

items.subject: HG-E111
items.text: Individual visit added because the patient became anxious during group and needed grounding and review of coping strategies. Patient reported feeling overwhelmed by workplace demands discussed in group and worry about returning to work. Work was narrowed to drafting two sentences to a supervisor, with no requirement to send today. Patient denied current suicidal thoughts; no acute safety concern identified.

items.subject: HG-E112
items.text: Individual video psychotherapy addressed the patient's hesitation about sending a message about a possible gradual return to work, including checking the draft repeatedly, and practiced choosing a planned time to send it. Sleep routine was discussed after a mixed night of sleep. Connection was lost for 10 minutes and resumed under the same appointment; the patient was engaged and restated the agreed task with no urgent safety concern reported.

items.subject: HG-E113
items.text: Skills group addressed translating a broad intention into one observable action; members practiced reducing a complicated task to a completable action and identifying a prompting cue. Patient used opening a work calendar as an example and voiced concern that seeing outstanding items would be overwhelming; facilitator encouraged a limited, planned review period and a stopping point. Patient contributed an example after the break.

items.subject: HG-E114
items.text: Professional-only care coordination call between Mira Patel, LCSW, and outside social worker Daniel Shaw, with a release on file, about practical supports for a gradual return to work. No patient contact occurred, no employment determination was made, and no change to medication or psychotherapy frequency was made.

items.subject: HG-E115
items.text: Individual psychotherapy addressing the patient's hesitation to respond to a supervisor's request for next-step discussion, with rehearsal of a brief response and a grounding cue. Sleep remained uneven and avoidance and bedtime routine continued as focus areas. No current suicidal ideation was reported.

items.subject: HG-E115
items.text: Individual in-person psychotherapy addressing difficulty moving from a supervisor's reply to arranging the next conversation, with anticipatory overwhelm about work issues. Rehearsed a specific, brief conversation request and a grounding exercise; patient remained uncertain about using the cue independently when anxious. Presentation consistent with ongoing anxiety, low mood, and functional difficulty around work demands; plan to continue individual and group work.

items.subject: HG-E116
items.text: Unsigned auto-generated template draft only; no clinician-documented session content. Charge CH-116 for group psychotherapy (1 group session) posted 2026-01-27 18:06.

items.subject: HG-E118
items.text: Skills group reviewed setbacks when practicing approach behaviors; members identified an initial effort, follow-through difficulties, and an adjustment. Patient reported opening the work calendar but delaying a follow-up conversation; facilitator helped identify a specific question to ask. Patient participated in paired rehearsal and accepted feedback about keeping requests brief.

items.subject: HG-E119
items.text: Patient's partner Casey attended first and discussed uncertainty about when reminders helped or increased Rowan's pressure; Rowan was not present for the first 15 minutes. Rowan joined at 13:15 and, with Casey, identified a pattern of reminders about contacting work leading to withdrawal, rehearsed requesting a specific kind of help, and agreed to one planned check-in. Rowan remained anxious but could explain the first step and found a limited plan more manageable. Plan: continue current outpatient treatment plan and revisit the communication pattern.

items.subject: HG-E120
items.text: Medication management follow-up for Rowan Mercer. Regimen, adherence, tolerability, and interval symptoms reviewed; patient denied current suicidal thoughts and no new acute safety issue emerged. No medication change made; continue current regimen with monitoring. No separately documented psychotherapy was provided.
